analysis:
Both units are head-side excerpts of docs/architecture/inference.md, a documentation-only change. The patch excerpt shows a date bump, a new paragraph on cluster service health-file separation (service-health.json vs part-health.json via DARKBLOOM_CLUSTER_MEMBER_HEALTH_FILE), and rewording of the cluster runtime-facts section so signed releases compute and register approval digests. The supplied units (lines 3999-4490) contain neither of those changed hunks. They carry only unchanged surrounding text on GLM/Qwen tensor-parallel, prefix SSD record encoding, media ingress and GPT-OSS/Gemma paging.

I found no change to code, authorization, attestation, encryption, trust boundaries or data exposure. The excerpt describes sealed AES-256-GCM all-sum and authenticated records, fail-closed load agreements, and per-tenant prefix partitions. That is consistent with T-041 (cache scoping and encrypted SSD) and does not weaken any threat-model assumption. I saw no new at-rest artifact and no TTL or scope change, so I raised no T-041 sign-off concern.

Open integration questions are limited to the hunks outside these units. The cluster_runtime digest registration claim in the provider-release process concerns how a release computes and registers approval digests. The health-file PID guard is described only in the patch excerpt, which is truncated (patch_excerpt_complete=false). Those descriptions would need a check against the actual code and the platform-owned release registration if code changes accompany them, but no code is supplied here. This is not evidence of a regression.
